content.text:
**Finding: COMPLIANT (preferred level).**

The Agreement contains no minimum purchase commitment, take-or-pay, shortfall payment, or volume cap on Ono:

- **§9.1(a)/§9.4(b)** — supply is framed as satisfying "Ono's requirements," and Ono "shall have the right to obtain" commercial Materials; it is a right, not an obligation.
- **§9.4(a)** — Ono expressly has "the right (but not the obligation) to Manufacture" or source its own requirements, with a Know-How transfer to enable it, and Array's supply duties then terminate.
- **§9.3(a)** — clinical Materials are procured only "as reasonably requested in writing by Ono," priced at cost/pass-through transfer price, i.e. pay-for-what-is-ordered.
- **§6.3** — the only recurring payment is a royalty on Annual Net Sales; there is no minimum annual royalty or true-up penalty.

Noted for the file (not a deviation): §9.3(a) and §9.4(b)(i) contemplate future clinical/commercial supply agreements containing "forecasting and ordering procedures." Those are agreements-to-agree and impose no present commitment, but binding-forecast liability is the likely place exposure would arise, so we should apply this rule again when those supply agreements are negotiated.

No redline proposed.
